_comment: P3-E E5 — the ONE authority of published-contract maturity.
This is contractual policy, not roadmap state and not an operational status. It answers
exactly one question per published module: may its public ABI change, and under what
conditions. It is deliberately NOT DSL_SURFACE_MANIFEST: that manifest classifies
constructors in the pipeline authoring surface, and this classifies the artifacts an
external CONSUMER compiles against. Reusing it would conflate a DSL function with a
library ABI and quietly make the stricter policy apply to the wrong surface.
Taxonomy (the canonical one; nothing outside it is accepted):
STABLE                 breaking is forbidden except across an explicit major boundary
PARTIAL                additive changes allowed; breaking needs a recorded exception
EXPERIMENTAL           breaking allowed under a recorded decision with a stated boundary
DEPRECATED             members may be removed only after the declared removal boundary
UNSUPPORTED_FAIL_CLOSED the construct refuses itself; there is no compatibility surface
Consumed by P3EPublishedContractMaturityFitnessTest, which fails the build when a module
published from build.gradle.kts has no entry here. A deliberate breaking change is recorded,
not discussed, in the SIBLING file published-contract-exceptions.json: one entry per break,
carrying the module, the commit sha, the surface, the change, the permitting maturity, the
reasoning and the removal boundary. This pointer used to read "See publishedContractExceptions()
in the same test", which named a function that does not exist and sent the reader to the
wrong file for a ledger that was one directory away.
P3-E E6 — SURFACES. A module is not one thing. `contracts` above is the module-level DEFAULT,
and it exists because a flat EXPERIMENTAL on every module is not a decision: it is a blanket
that lets the next change ride on it without saying what it is riding on. `surfaces` below is
where the guarantee genuinely DIFFERS from the module default, and a surface entry must beat
the module on evidence or not exist.
Resolution is: effective(module, surface) = surfaces[module][surface] if declared, else the
module's own classification. Nothing is inherited implicitly and nothing is inferred from the
package name.
The four rules that make this executable rather than decorative, all enforced by the fitness
test:
1. `covers` must resolve in BOTH independent authorities — the module's published .api dump
and DSL_SURFACE_MANIFEST.md. One authority alone is forgeable: the ABI proves the symbol
ships, the manifest proves what it means. A family that names something invented in
either file fails the build.
2. A surface may be STRICTER than its module. It may not be MORE PERMISSIVE. Refinement that
loosens the policy is not refinement, it is an escape hatch with a longer name.
3. An exception may not invoke a maturity looser than the effective one at its surface.
4. UNSUPPORTED_FAIL_CLOSED hosts no exceptions, because a construct that refuses itself has
nothing a consumer could have depended on. That is the whole meaning of the classification.

pipeline-domain: EXPERIMENTAL, and the reason is specific rather than convenient: this module is the
innermost seam and its types are re-exported through pipeline-events and
pipeline-scripting-api, so almost every change to it is additive-by-necessity rather
than by choice. The one class of change this repository made repeatedly in P3-E is
enriching an internal decision ADT with evidence the producer already had
(WaitUntilReconciliationDecision.Aborted gained the attempt it had been discarding into
a string). That is a real breaking change to a published data class, and pretending
otherwise would make the classification a description of what we wish were true.
Promoting it to STABLE requires that the decision ADTs stop being part of the external
surface — i.e. that consumers resolve outcomes through event projections rather than
reaching for domain ADTs directly. That is S5.4's work, and until it lands the honest
pipeline-scripting-api: EXPERIMENTAL: the DSL is the authored authoring surface and several of its constructs
are already deprecated with a declared replacement (catchError, LFC1-007), which is the
signature of a surface still converging.
pipeline-events: EXPERIMENTAL: the wire vocabulary is published and load-bearing, and this block is
actively changing it (typed projections, fail-closed decoders). It is not a frozen
contract yet, and calling it one would only defer the work.
pipeline-output: EXPERIMENTAL: the smallest of the four and the least consumed; nothing in the P3-E

guarantee: These four are ACCEPTED SYNTAX THAT ALWAYS FAILS CLOSED, and they are the only
published surfaces in this repository where that is true.
The manifest pins each one: `git` and `load` are ATOMIC_STEP with no handler and no
descriptor row, so admission rejects before any effect; `node` and `ansiColor` lower to
core.node / core.ansiColor with no descriptor row, so compile/validate rejects; the
`retry` retrofit points at the block form and throws IllegalArgumentException.
Why they are not merely EXPERIMENTAL, which is what the module says as a whole: there is
no consumer program that can contain a working call to any of them. Compatibility is a
relation between a shipped artifact and a caller that got a value out of it. A construct
whose every call path ends in a refusal has no such caller, so there is nothing to freeze
and nothing to break. Calling that EXPERIMENTAL would be exactly the blanket this layer
exists to replace — it would promise a stability guarantee for a guarantee that does not
The practical consequence is the direction that matters: removing or reshaping these four
does NOT need a recorded exception, while touching any other surface of
promotion_precondition: Promotion here means IMPLEMENTING, not re-describing. The classification stops being
UNSUPPORTED_FAIL_CLOSED on the day the construct acquires a handler, a descriptor row and
an interpreter that can succeed — the same three things `agent` needed before it left
this state in S3.1. Promoting it without them would be classifying a stub as a contract.
